accelerated.label: 5% on Amazon, BookMyShow, Cult.fit, Flipkart, Myntra, Sony LIV, Swiggy, Tata CLiQ, Uber, Zomato
accelerated.notes: Needs the merchant's own terminal/merchant ID. Non-EMI only. MCC 6540 never earns 5%. Uber earns 5% only on MCC 4121. Purchases through SmartBuy or PayZapp earn 1%. Gift/prepaid card and voucher purchases on these merchants earn 1%.

exclusions.notes: Education through third-party apps earns nothing since 1 Sep 2024 (direct to school/college site or POS still earns). Rent and government earn nothing since 1 Jan 2023. EMI (even if closed early) and wallet loads earn nothing since 1 Sep 2024.

card_reward_rules.baseCapNote: 1% category has its own 1,000 CashPoint cap, separate from the 5% cap
card_reward_rules.source: HDFC Millennia T&C (published 20 Jul 2026, sections 25 Apr 2025)

info.postedOn: first week of the next calendar month, by settlement/posting date

redemption.statementCredit: 1 CashPoint = Rs 1; minimum 500 CashPoints; Rs 50 fee per redemption; max 3,000 points per calendar month
redemption.smartBuyFlightsHotels: 1 CashPoint = Rs 0.30, up to 50% of the booking, 50,000 points per month cap
redemption.catalogue: Rs 99 + tax handling fee per request; up to 70% of voucher value in points

benefits: Welcome: 1,000 CashPoints when the joining fee is paid; nothing on renewal fee
Quarterly milestone: Rs 1 lakh net spend in a calendar quarter gives a Rs 1,000 voucher (SMS within 30 working days, valid 120 days); EMI principal counts, SmartEMI/Dial an EMI does not
1% fuel surcharge waiver on Rs 400 to Rs 5,000, up to Rs 250 per statement cycle
Domestic lounge access removed from 1 Dec 2023

feesAndCharges.rentOrEducationViaThirdPartyApps: 1% fee, capped Rs 3,000 per transaction (from 1 Aug 2024)
feesAndCharges.fuelAbove15000PerTxn: 1% on the whole amount, capped Rs 3,000
feesAndCharges.utilitiesAbove50000PerTxn: 1% on the whole amount, capped Rs 3,000 (insurance is not utility)
feesAndCharges.overlimit: 2.5% of the overlimit amount, minimum Rs 550
feesAndCharges.financeCharge: 3.75% a month (45% a year) for most variants

accelerated.label: 10% on the Swiggy app: Food, Instamart, Dineout
accelerated.notes: Minimum Rs 249 per transaction from 21 Apr 2026. Swiggy Money wallet, Swiggy Liquor and Swiggy Minis do not count. Matched on the merchant and terminal IDs.

accelerated.label: 5% on select online merchants (apparel, electronics, department stores, pet, home decor, personal care, local cabs, entertainment, pharmacies, discount stores)
accelerated.notes: Online only, and only select merchants under these MCCs. MCC 5411 (grocery) counts only for Amazon and Flipkart (from 10 May 2025). Grocery and gift cards on other merchants earn nothing. Cleartrip earns 5% by merchant name from 17 Apr 2026.

exclusions.notes: Once a purchase is converted to EMI the cashback is reversed in the next statement, even if the EMI is later foreclosed. The Swiggy HDFC T&C does not list education, so do not exclude it here (the pasted summary did).

card_reward_rules.roundingNote: Terms say nearest rupee per transaction, but the worked example rounds 6.5 down to 6. Treat .5 as down.
card_reward_rules.source: Swiggy HDFC Bank Credit Card T&C (published 18 Sep 2026)

accelerated.label: 5% on online spends
accelerated.notes: Online is decided by the network's online indicator, not by the merchant. Anything not flagged online is offline. FinPing has no online/offline flag on a transaction yet, so add merchant words (amazon, flipkart...) to this rule for it to apply; everything else is paid the 1% offline rate.

categories: Standing instructions or Fetch and Pay on SBI platforms
exclusions.notes: Cashback reversed on EMI conversion in the same statement month; a foreclosed EMI never gives it back. Refunds reverse the cashback. A reversal after the cap was reached cannot be used to earn more.

accelerated.label: 10% on dining, food delivery, grocery, shopping and utilities
accelerated.notes: Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra stay at 1.5%. Cashback is by MCC only. The Bank's classification is final. The MCC table in the PDF is laid out in columns that extract out of order, so verify the shopping codes against the PDF before relying on them. Cap Rs 1,200 per month. Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra purchases earn 1.5% and are not eligible for the 10%. Cashback depends on the merchant category the bank assigns to the transaction.

exclusions.notes: International spends no longer earn 1.5% because the forex mark-up is 1.99%. Instant EMI is treated as a loan and earns nothing. Cashback on reversed or cancelled spends is recovered from the next statement. Toll, cash withdrawals, card repayments, foreign currency, crypto, broker, wholesale club and local bus and metro spends are excluded by merchant code; the app's categories cannot tell all of these apart.
excludedSpendTypes: Cash withdrawals and credit card repayments
Foreign currency, liquid and cryptocurrency purchases

card_reward_rules.capPeriodNote: The page says Rs 1,200 per month; the bank credits it by statement cycle, so the cap follows the billing cycle

info.postedOn: within 45 days of the statement date (illustration: statement 2nd, credit on the 17th of the following month)
benefits: Lounge: 3 complimentary visits a year (2 domestic, one per 6 months; 1 international from 1 Sep 2026)

feesAndCharges.annualFeeWaiver: spend of Rs 2,00,000 a year; fee reversed in the next statement after the anniversary year
feesAndCharges.financeCharge: 3.75% a month (45% a year), from the date of transaction
feesAndCharges.lateFee: 100% of minimum due, minimum Rs 250 and maximum Rs 1,200 a month; charged if not paid within 3 days of the due date
feesAndCharges.cashAdvance: 1% processing fee plus taxes (HSBC key fact statement)
feesAndCharges.forexMarkupNote: The earlier text (3.5% on the Platinum cards) is about HSBC's other cards, not Live+
feesAndCharges.fuelSurcharge: No waiver. A 1% fuel surcharge applies
feesAndCharges.cashAdvanceConflict: Card Insider (29 Jul 2026) says 2.5% with a minimum of Rs 500. The bank's own key fact statement is kept above; check your statement.

forex.note: Low forex markup on international spends (entry-level cashback cards usually charge about 3.5%).
forex.cashbackNote: International spends do NOT earn the 1.5% unlimited cashback, even with the lower markup. The app cannot tell international from domestic spends, so such a spend may show the 1.5% rate; the bank will not credit it.

welcome.name: Welcome cashback
welcome.condition: Log in to the HSBC India Mobile Banking app and spend Rs 25,000 within 30 days of card issuance.

welcome.name: Welcome voucher (limited-time Visa offer)
welcome.condition: Activate the card with one transaction of Rs 300 or more. Voucher for Amazon Pay, Zomato or Swiggy.

lounge.domesticRule: One visit every six months, at participating lounges in India
lounge.internationalRule: Through the Visa Airport Companion Program (from 1 Sep 2026 per the service guide)

details.movieOffer: Buy 1 Get 1 free on movie tickets, up to Rs 200 off the second ticket
details.cashbackPosting: Credited as cashback within 45 days after the statement is generated; no points to redeem; redemption fee nil

liveReserve.summary: Curated dining and lifestyle programme for activated Live+ cardholders, run with Times Prime
liveReserve.diningRules: Only one dining benefit (set menu, beverage or dessert) per table per reservation; subject to availability, blackout dates and each restaurant's terms; the food bill is paid at the restaurant
lifestyleBrands: other partners on the Live+ Reserve portal
liveReserve.brandsNote: The list of partners can change during the offer period
howToRedeem: Open the Live+ Reserve portal (dinewithtimesprime.com/hsbcliveplus) after activating the card
Verify the registered mobile number with an OTP
Complete a Rs 1 verification transaction with the Live+ card
Browse restaurants or lifestyle offers and book or redeem

pros: Cashback, lounge access, Visa Infinite benefits and the Live+ Reserve for a Rs 999 + GST annual fee
10% cashback on utility bills (up to Rs 1,200 a month), which many cashback cards no longer give
cons: Many merchant categories are excluded; the merchant category assigned by the bank decides
